name: DFRobot FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C6
//chip: DFRobot wiki DFR1075, Board Overview: 'ESP32-C6FH4 MCU' - the chip with 4 MB flash in its package, a QFN32 (ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, cover page). No module: the chip sits on the board.
//micropython_port: The MicroPython build this board runs. NOT fetched in this round: carried from spark's own xiao-esp32-c6.json, which names https://micropython.org/download/ESP32_GENERIC_C6/ for the same chip. DFRobot's wiki links a MicroPython tutorial but names no board-specific build.
//: Copied from spark's firebeetle2-esp32s3.json on 2026-10-09 and rewritten for the C6 from DFRobot's and Espressif's documents. Round 0 of P100: nothing here has touched hardware.
//sku: DFR1075, the one SKU DFRobot sells as FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C6 (wiki title). DFR1117 (Beetle ESP32-C6), DFR1222/DFR1287 (FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C5) are different boards.
//sources: Every fact below came from one of these. The Arduino variant header is the authority for the pin names; DFRobot's dimension drawing and schematic for the pads; soc_caps.h and the chip datasheet for what the silicon can do.

sources.capabilities: espressif/esp-idf v5.5.2 components/soc/esp32c6/include/soc/soc_caps.h; ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5

//physical: Every number here is from DFRobot's dimension drawing [DFR1075][V1.1.0], dated 20231025, a vector PDF with no text layer. The pad and hole centres were parsed geometrically from its paths (scale from the 60.00 mm board outline, 762.72 pt = 60.00 mm, 12.712 pt/mm); the labels were read off a render of the same drawing, so the label-to-pad assignment is 'from a picture', cross-checked against the V1.1 schematic's headers P1 and P2, which agree pad for pad.

physical.//footprint_module: A name chosen here for the module emit_footprint.py writes; not a vendor fact.
physical.//width_mm: stated: dimension drawing '25.40mm' and wiki 'Dimension 25.4x60mm'. Measured on the drawing's outline: 25.38 mm.
physical.//height_mm: stated: dimension drawing '60.00mm' and wiki '25.4x60mm'. Used as the scale reference for every other measurement here.
physical.//thickness_mm: stated: dimension drawing's PCB Information table, 'Thickness: 1.6mm'.
physical.//corner_radius_mm: measured from the drawing: the straight edges stop 19.08 pt (1.50 mm) and 19.44 pt (1.53 mm) short of the corners. Not stated by DFRobot.

header.//rows: stated: the drawing shows two rows; the schematic has P2 (18 pins) and P1 (14 pins).
header.//pins: stated: schematic V1.1 P2 is 1x18, P1 is 1x14; the drawing has 18 and 14 pads.
header.//pitch_mm: measured from the drawing: 18 pad centres from x = 119.10 pt to 667.98 pt, 17 pitches, 32.287 pt = 2.5399 mm. Not stated as a number by DFRobot.
header.//row_spacing_mm: measured from the drawing: the through-hole circles of the two rows are 290.4 pt apart = 22.845 mm, i.e. 22.86 (9 pitches) within the drawing's 0.36 pt quantisation. The castellated half-holes on the edges are 323.88 pt = 25.48 mm apart; as on the S3, the through-holes are the ones a header mates with.
header.//drill_mm: NOT stated: the dimension drawing draws each pad as two 1.50 mm circles (the edge half-hole and the through-hole) and no drill. No number recorded rather than a guessed one.
header.//pad_mm: measured from the drawing: every pad circle is 19.08 pt = 1.501 mm across.
header.//alignment: Both rows are flush at the end away from USB-C; the 18-pin row runs four pitches further toward the USB end (drawing: both rows start at x = 119.10 pt, the 14-pin row ends at 538.86 pt, the 18-pin row at 667.98 pt). The same arrangement as the S3's file, so flush_edge is kept as that file has it.
header.//first_pad_from_edge_mm: measured from the drawing: first pad centre x = 119.10 pt, flush board edge x = 53.04 pt, 66.06 pt = 5.197 mm.

mounting_holes.//diameter_mm: measured from the drawing: each hole circle is 25.44 pt across = 2.001 mm.
mounting_holes.//inset_mm: measured from the drawing: hole centres 1.699 mm from the short edges and 1.694 mm from the long edges.
mounting_holes.//spacing_x_mm: stated: drawing '22.00mm' between the holes across the board; measured 21.98 mm.
mounting_holes.//spacing_y_mm: stated: drawing '56.60mm' between the holes along the board; measured 56.60 mm.

physical.//max_component_height: NOT stated by DFRobot for this board; the STP file was not opened. No number recorded.
physical.//wokwi_size_px: Copied unchanged from the S3's file, whose outline is the same 25.4 x 60 mm. A picture size, not a measurement.
physical.//header_order: Which silkscreen label sits on which PAD, per row, from the end away from USB-C. Read off the dimension drawing (from a picture of it) and checked against the V1.1 schematic: P2 pin 18..1 = 17,16,8,14,NC,1,18,9,19,20,21,22,23,NC,GND,NC,3V3,RST and P1 pin 14..1 = NC,7,6,15,NC,2,3,4,5,SDA,SCL,GND,3V3,VCC. The silkscreen prints GPIO NUMBERS, not D-labels; pad_aliases below bridges pins_arduino.h's names to them. Five pads are silkscreened NC and are numbered here NC1..NC5 so every pad has its own name; GND and 3V3 appear on both rows and are numbered the same way (GND1/GND2, 3V3/3V3_2). The pad silkscreened VIN is net VCC in the schematic. GPIO19 and GPIO20 are brought out TWICE: as 19/20 on the 18-pin row and as SDA/SCL on the 14-pin row (schematic: P2-10 IO19/SDA, P2-9 IO20/SCL, P1-5 IO19/SDA, P1-4 IO20/SCL).

header_order.//: 18-pin row first, then the 14-pin row; each from the end away from the USB-C.

physical.//pad_aliases: Where a pin's NAME in `pins` differs from the label silkscreened on its PAD. On this board every Arduino name differs: the silkscreen prints the GPIO number. SDA and SCL have pads of their own name; the second pads of the same GPIOs, 19 and 20, have no name in pins_arduino.h and so no entry here.

//wokwi_part_type: NOT fetched in this round (Wokwi's pages are outside the round's allowed sources). Wokwi has no FireBeetle 2 C6 part as far as this file knows; the generic ESP32-C6 devkit is named from memory as the same-silicon stand-in. Check against wokwi/wokwi-boards before trusting it.
//wokwi_pin_naming: Assumed to be by raw GPIO number, as the S3 devkit stand-in's is. Not verified for the C6 devkit.
//wokwi_power_pins: UNVERIFIED: the stand-in's power pin names follow the S3 devkit's pattern from spark's S3 file; nobody has read the C6 devkit's names. Keyed by the name the footprint gives the pad.
//power_pads: Which pad carries which rail, and which way it flows. From the V1.1 schematic: 3V3 (P1-2, P2-2) is the TPS62A02's output (V1.1) or the HM6245's (V1.0); the pad silkscreened VIN is net VCC, which reaches VCC1 through Q1, an AO3407 P-FET whose gate is pulled to ground by R11 (2k) and lifted by VUSB, so USB power turns the path from VIN off. VCC1 feeds both the CN3165 solar charger and, through D4 (SS34), the 3.3 V regulator. The second 3V3 pad carries the same rail; only the first names the supply figures, so the rail is not counted twice.

VIN.//: DFRobot wiki: 'VIN 5 V DC input or 5 V solar panel'. Unlike the S3's VCC, feeding it charges the battery (power.feeding_vin_charges_the_battery). Through a P-FET and a Schottky, not a short; DFRobot rate neither.

//pins: Arduino names and the GPIO each is, from pins_arduino.h. The silkscreen prints the GPIO number itself (see header_order). D0, D1, D4, D5, D8, D10, D14 and A0 do not exist in the variant header. SS and A4 are both GPIO5; SDA and SCL are on two pads each.
//wake_capable_gpio: GPIO0-7: soc_caps.h (ESP-IDF v5.5.2) SOC_RTCIO_PIN_COUNT = 8, and the datasheet v1.5 Table 2-7 (page 22) lists LP_GPIO0..LP_GPIO7 on pins 6-13 = GPIO0-7. On this header that is 1 (D6), 2 (A1), 3 (A2), 4 (A3), 5 (A4), 6 (D12), 7 (D11); GPIO0 is the battery-voltage divider, not on the header.
//adc_gpio: ADC1 channels 0-6 on GPIO0-6: datasheet v1.5 Table 2-9 (page 23); soc_caps.h SOC_ADC_PERIPH_NUM 1, SOC_ADC_MAX_CHANNEL_NUM 7; wiki '1 x 12-bit SAR ADC, 7 Channel'. The C6 has no ADC2, so there is no WiFi caveat. GPIO0 is wired on board to the battery divider (R15/R16 1M/1M, ADC_BAT) and is not on the header.
//pin_roles: What a pin IS, beyond its number. A pin with a role is usable with a caveat, and the caveat is the note.
//pin_roles_not_read_by_spark: Not a role spark reads (boards.py --validate refused it); kept as a note. GPIO 4, 5, 6, 7: Datasheet v1.5 page 25: 'GPIO4, GPIO5, GPIO6, GPIO7: JTAG interface' (MTMS, MTDI, MTCK, MTDO). Usable as GPIO when the USB Serial/JTAG (GPIO12/13, not on the header) is used for debugging. | Not a role spark reads (boards.py --validate refused it); kept as a note. GPIO 15, 23, 22, 21, 8, 14, 1, 18, 6, 20, 19, 7: Also wired to the on-board GDI display FPC (wiki 'GDI Display Interface'; pins_arduino.h GDI_* defines; schematic P3). Free while no display is plugged in. The wiki's table writes INT as '7/D1'; pins_arduino.h names GPIO7 D11.

strapping.note: Datasheet v1.5 section 2.3 (page 25): 'GPIO4, GPIO5, GPIO8, GPIO9, GPIO15: Strapping pins.' On this header: A3 (4), A4 (5), D2 (8), D9 (9, the BOOT button, 10k pull-up R1 to 3V3) and D13 (15, the on-board LED). Nothing may hold GPIO9 low at reset, or the chip enters the bootloader.

onboard_led.note: LED_BUILTIN = 15 in pins_arduino.h; schematic V1.1: GPIO15 drives D1 through R5 (2k) to ground. Silkscreened 15 (D13). It lights whatever you put on it, and it is a strapping pin.

onboard_button.note: The BOOT button S1 (schematic V1.1: IO9/Boot to ground, R1 10k pull-up). Silkscreened 9 (D9). Held at reset it enters the bootloader; it cannot wake the chip from deep sleep.

not_wake_capable.note: Outside GPIO0-7 (soc_caps.h SOC_RTCIO_PIN_COUNT 8), so these header pins cannot wake the chip.

console_uart.note: U0TXD and U0RXD (schematic V1.1: U0TXD through R13 499R to IO16/TX; U0RXD to IO17/RX). The ROM bootloader prints on TX at every reset.

spi.note: MOSI, MISO, SCK and SS from pins_arduino.h, silkscreened 22, 21, 23 and 5. Taken last, as on the S3.

i2c.note: SDA and SCL from pins_arduino.h; each is on two pads (19/SDA, 20/SCL). No pull-ups on the V1.1 schematic: every I2C device brings its own.

//deep_sleep: How this chip is woken. soc_caps.h (ESP-IDF v5.5.2) defines SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT1_WAKEUP and SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT1_WAKEUP_MODE_PER_PIN, and does NOT define SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT0_WAKEUP, so esp32.wake_on_ext0 does not exist on this chip and there is no single_pin_api.

deep_sleep.//single_polarity_for_all_pins: True of MicroPython's API, not of the silicon (the silicon has a level per pin, per soc_caps.h above). The MicroPython half is carried from spark's xiao-esp32-c6.json (modesp32.c v1.29.0), not re-read in this round.
deep_sleep.//simulated_by_wokwi: Carried from spark's xiao-esp32-c6.json: established there by experiment on the C6, Wokwi wakes from a timer but not from a GPIO. Not retested on the C6 devkit stand-in.

//vendor: Where the pin map can be re-derived from. check_vendor_pins.py fetches this header and compares.
//hardware_revisions: One SKU, more than one power design. DFRobot's own documents name the revisions three ways: the wiki's component table says HM6245 LDO 'V1.0' and TPS62A02 'V1.1'; its sleep-current row says 'Version 1.0' and 'Version 1.2'; the schematics zip holds 'V1.0 Schematics.pdf' (HM6245P3V3PR, title block dated 2023/10/25) and 'V1.1 Schematics.pdf' (TPS62A02DRLR, dated 2024/12/6). The dimension drawing is [V1.1.0], dated 20231025. Which revision a given board is, is read off its regulator.

hardware_revisions.how_to_tell: The 3.3 V regulator: an HM6245 LDO is the earlier board, a TPS62A02 buck the later one (wiki Board Overview). Package markings were not checked.

v1_0.3v3_regulator: HM6245P3V3PR LDO (schematic 'V1.0'); current rating not read - its datasheet was not fetched

v1_1.3v3_regulator: TPS62A02DRLR buck (schematic 'V1.1'); current rating not read - TI's datasheet was not fetched
v1_1.i2c_pullups: NONE on IO19/IO20 in the V1.1 schematic, read from a render of it

//documents: The documents this record's facts rest on, as fetched on 2026-10-09 in round 0 of P100. They sit in the round's scratch folder, NOT kept in a spark store: the five steps keep nothing. sha256 of the file as downloaded.
//power: What DFRobot document, and what only the chip datasheet says. DFRobot publish no current rating for either rail.

vin_reaches_vcc1_through_a_pfet.source: DFRobot schematic V1.1: VCC (the VIN pad) - Q1 AO3407 - VCC1; gate to VUSB, R11 2k to ground
vin_reaches_vcc1_through_a_pfet.note: Read once from a render of the schematic. With USB plugged in, VUSB reaches VCC1 through D2 (SS34) and Q1 is off.

power.//charge_current_a: stated: wiki 'Max Charging Current 0.5A'. The V1.1 schematic's own note reads 'ICH = 1188V / R9 = 540mA' with R9 = 2.2k: calculated 1188/2200 = 0.54 A.

charge_current_a.source: DFRobot wiki DFR1075 'Max Charging Current 0.5A'; schematic V1.1 CN3165, R9 2.2k, 'ICH = 1188V / R9 = 540mA'

feeding_vin_charges_the_battery.source: DFRobot wiki: 'VCC Input Voltage 5V DC or 5V Solar Panel', 'solar (MPPT for max solar output)'; schematic V1.1: VCC1 is the CN3165 charger's VIN

regulator_3v3_a.source: Not read: DFRobot rate neither regulator, and neither the HM6245 nor the TPS62A02 datasheet was fetched in this round.
regulator_3v3_a.why_it_matters: What everything on 3V3 is summed against, the chip's own radio included.

power.//module_peak_a: datasheet-max (a peak): ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-7 (page 66): 802.11b, 1 Mbps, DSSS @ 21.0 dBm, 354 mA peak.

module_peak_a.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-7 (page 66): 802.11b, 1 Mbps, DSSS @ 21.0 dBm TX, 354 mA peak
module_peak_a.note: The chip is on the board directly (ESP32-C6FH4), so the chip's figure is the 'module' figure.

power.//deep_sleep_ua: stated: wiki 'Sleep Current (Deep Sleep Mode, Battery-Powered) Version 1.0: 16uA, Version 1.2: 36uA'; the higher is recorded because one file covers both. The chip alone: datasheet v1.5 Table 5-11 (page 68), Deep-sleep 7 uA typ.

deep_sleep_ua.source: DFRobot wiki DFR1075 Specification: Version 1.0 16 uA, Version 1.2 36 uA (battery-powered, deep sleep). Chip alone 7 uA typ, ESP32-C6 datasheet v1.5 Table 5-11, page 68.
deep_sleep_ua.why_it_matters: Battery life of a sleeping gadget. Board-level and stated by the vendor, not measured here.

power.//io_volts: datasheet-typ: Table 5-2 (page 64) VDDPST1/VDDPST2 3.0 min, 3.3 typ, 3.6 max V; Table 5-4 (page 65) VOH >= 0.8 x VDD, IOH 40 mA typ at VOH >= 2.64 V, PAD_DRIVER = 3.

io_volts.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-2 (page 64): VDDPST1/VDDPST2 3.0 min, 3.3 typ, 3.6 max V; Table 5-4 (page 65): VOH >= 0.8 x VDD; IOH 40 mA typ at VOH >= 2.64 V
io_volts.why_it_matters: the voltage a GPIO drives, from which a series resistor's value is computed
